paragraph: PROPHET TO ISRAEL IN THE DAYS OF UZZIAH AND JEROBOAM SON OF JOASH · TWO KINGDOMS

blocks.text: PROPHET TO ISRAEL IN THE DAYS OF UZZIAH AND JEROBOAM SON OF JOASH · TWO KINGDOMS
Amos. A herdman of Tekoa in Judah, sent to prophesy at Beth-el in the northern kingdom.
“And the LORD took me as I followed the flock, and the LORD said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel”
The book is “The words of Amos ... which he saw concerning Israel”. Amos 1:1
Five visions are told in the first person, three of them opening “Thus hath the Lord GOD shewed unto me”. Amos 7:1 Amos 7:4 Amos 7:7 Amos 8:1 Amos 9:1
He prophesied at Beth-el, “the king's chapel”, and Amaziah told him to flee into Judah and prophesy there. Amos 7:10–13
He says the prophet cannot keep silent: “the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” Amos 3:7–8
“I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword”
The word in its main themes
“The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem”
“they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes”
“But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream”
“Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live”
The day of the LORD is darkness
“Woe unto you that desire the day of the LORD! to what end is it for you? the day of the LORD is darkness, and not light”
“prepare to meet thy God, O Israel”
“In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen”
To whom the word was spoken
“because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron”
“because they carried away captive the whole captivity, to deliver them up to Edom”
“because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant”
“because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity”
“because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border”
“because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime”
“because they have despised the law of the LORD, and have not kept his commandments”
“because they sold the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of shoes”
TO “YE KINE OF BASHAN” IN THE MOUNTAIN OF SAMARIA
“Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy”
“Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword”
1 The LORD roars from Zion Amos 1:1–2
2 For three transgressions, and for four: the nations, Judah and Israel Amos 1:3–2:16
3 Hear this word: Samaria's sins and the woes Amos 3:1–6:14
4 Five visions, and Amaziah at Beth-el Amos 7:1–9:10
5 The tabernacle of David raised up Amos 9:11–15
WHERE THE NEW TESTAMENT QUOTES IT · 2
Each band joins a chapter of Amos to the New Testament book quoting it (one book).
Who stood with him, and against him
Amaziah told Amos to flee to Judah and “eat bread, and prophesy there”. Amos answered with a word against Amaziah. Scripture does not say whether Amos left, or how or where he died. Amos 7:12–17

The Lives of the Prophets, attributed to Epiphanius, tells that Amos was killed by a blow on the temple struck by Amaziah, priest of Beth-el.[18] Who says so: The pseudo-Epiphanian Lives of the Prophets, as reported in the Jewish Encyclopedia (1901), date of the Lives not given in the source read

A rabbinic tradition says King Uzziah killed Amos, striking him on the forehead with a glowing iron. The Jewish Encyclopedia gives it from Gedaliah ibn Yahya's Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah as quoted in the Seder ha-Dorot, and notes that the Venice edition of 1587 does not mention it.[18] Who says so: Rabbinic tradition, as reported in the Jewish Encyclopedia (1901) from Gedaliah ibn Yahya's Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah, no date given in the source read; the Jewish Encyclopedia notes that the Venice edition of 1587 lacks the story

Amos's words are dated “two years before the earthquake”, and Zechariah later recalls how the people “fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah”. Neither gives a year. Amos 1:1 Zechariah 14:5
Amos 1 Amos 2 Amos 3 Amos 4 Amos 5 Amos 6 Amos 7 Amos 8 Amos 9 Acts 7 Acts 15
Scripture does not say how long Amos prophesied, whether he left Beth-el when told to, or how he died.
Scripture does not tell how Jeroboam answered Amaziah's report.
